Counsel for Respondent :- Abhinav Gaur Hon'ble Prakash Padia,J.
Heard Sri Navin Sinha, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Sri Prateek Rai, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri Arvind Kumar Goswami put his appearance on behalf of respondent no. 1 and Sri Abhinav Gaur accepted notice on behalf of respondent nos. 2, 3 and 4.

The petitioner has preferred this present writ petition with the prayer to quash the order dated 25.09.2019 passed by Commissioner for Food Safety/Chief Executive Officer/respondent no. 3 by which the appeal preferred by the petitioner under section 32 (4) (a) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter called as Act '2006') was rejected.
It is argued by Sri Navin Sinha, learned Senior Advocate that the order impugned passed by the respondent no. 3 is absolutely non speaking order.
It is further argued that no reasons has been assigned by the respondent no. 3 by passing the order impugned.

sentences.text: the perusal of the record notice dated 06.05.2019 issued against the petitioner.
Challenging the aforesaid notice the appeal was preferred by the petitioner before respondent no. 3 as provided under section 32 (4) (c) of Food Safety and Standards act, 2006.
The aforesaid appeal preferred by the petitioner before the respondent no. 3 was rejected by him vide order dated 25.09.2019, copy of which is appended as (Annexure-1 to the writ petition).
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the present writ petition is being disposed of finally at the admission stage itself.
It appears from the perusal of the record that a notice dated 06.05.2019 was issued by the Food Director, Central Licence Authority, (Lucknow and Chandigarh Reason) FSS AI, to the present petitioner.
The aforesaid noitce was challenged by the petitioner by filing an appeal as provided under section 32 (4) (a) of the Act of 2006.

Under Section 32 of the Act 2006 it is provided that if the designated officer has reasonable ground for believing that any food business operator has failed to comply with any regualtions to which this section applies, he may issue a notice to the food business operator.
It is further provided under Sub Rule 4 that any person who is aggrieved by the notice may appeal to the Commissioner of Food Safety whose decision thereon, shall be final.

Section 32 of the Act of 2006 is reproduced below:-
32.
Improvement notices.

(1) If the Designated Officer has reasonable ground for believing that any food business operator has failed to comply with any regulations to which this section applies, he may, by a notice served on that food business operator (in this Act referred to as an "improvement notice")?
(a) state the grounds for believing that the food business operator has failed to comply with the regulations;

(b) specify the matters which constitute the food business operator's failure so to comply;
(c) specify the measures which, in the opinion of the said Authority, the food business operator must take, in order to secure compliance; and (d) require the food business operator to take those measures, or measures which are at least equivalent to them, within a reasonable period (not being less than fourteen days) as may be specified in the notice.
(2) If the food business operator fails to comply with an improvement notice, his licence may be suspended.

(3) If the food business operator still fails to comply with the improvement notice, the Designated Officer may, after giving the licensee an opportunity to shows cause, cancel the licence granted to M/S Tapan Agro Industries Pvt. sentences.text: The order passed by respondent no. 3 which is under challenged in the present writ petition is absolutely not speaking order.
Reason is the heart beat of every conclusion.
In the absence of reasons the order becomes lifeless.
Non recording of reasons renders the order to be violative of principles of natural justice.
Reasons ensures transparency and fairness in decision making.
It enables litigant to know reasons for acceptance or rejection of his prayer.
It is statutory requirement of natural justice.
Reasons are really linchpin to administration of justice.
It is link between the mind of the decision taker and the controversy in question.
Thus failure to give reasons amounts to denial of justice.

In view of the aforesaid, since no valid reasons have been recorded for the conclusion reached in the impugned order dated 25.09.2019 and as such it can not be sustained and, is therefore, quashed.
The writ petition is allowed.
Matter is remitted back to the respondent no.3 to pass an order afresh in accordance with law.

The order shall be passed by the respondent no.3 expeditiously, preferably within three months from today after affording reasonable opportunities of hearing to the petitioner without granting any unnecessary adjournment.
With the aforesaid observation the writ petition is allowed.
Order Date :- 1.10.2019
